videos.title: How to Get Stronger at Arm Wrestling (What Actually Works on the Table)
videos.summary:
How do you get stronger at arm wrestling?

It's the most searched question in our sport, and almost everyone answers it wrong. They chase heavier lifts. They try to make weak habits stronger. They run from the grip and call it technique.

Arm wrestling isn't a deadlift. You're not pulling against a bar. You're against another human, and that changes everything. The table is still the best place to get stronger — more than any gym session — if you train the right habits early.

The habit that kills potential is running: backing out of the grip, living on the fingers, hoping to float over the top. You lose side pressure. You lose control. You teach your body the wrong fight.

The habit that raises your ceiling is gripping deep. As high as you can be while still as deep as you can be. Hold on. Take the losses now. Full wrist, full pronation, full side pressure, full back. That's where real arm wrestling strength is built — and it's the only path that holds up when the humans across from you get serious.

Grip deep. Engage the fundamentals. That's how you get strong at this sport.

videos.title: Super Curl Bar Curls: How to Dominate the Ready Go in Armwrestling
videos.summary:
Most armwrestlers think bicep training is only for hookers. I see it differently.

The way I curl on a super curl bar puts my hands close together and slightly pronated, which is almost exactly how my hand is set at the ready go. That means the strength I build in the gym carries straight to the table, right where matches are won or lost.

In this video I break down why this curl helps you hold the centre, start every match with your hand inside your shoulder, and build the wrist stability and static back pressure that turns into side pressure your opponent can't handle. Win the centre, win the ready go, and you're halfway to winning the match.
